opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write access; admin only if their role owns the system, which is not the case here (Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ashley Roberts (E016) is a contractor with basic security training (note: HR lists full_time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type/training). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Ashley Roberts (E016) requested write access to Payroll. While HR lists the employee as full-time, the Security DB (authoritative for employment type/training per the Security agent) lists Ashley as a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

Ashley Roberts (E016) requests write access to Payroll.

HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write.

Security note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Security agent says Security DB is authoritative for employment type/training.

Policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

There is a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training. The Security agent claims their DB is authoritative. The policy says contractor with basic training: read max. Requested write is above max (read), so grant max = read.

Alternatively if we considered HR, full_time max is write, request write, grant write. But the Security note is authoritative for employment type/training, so contractor, basic training -> read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit decision with reason.
